# Thompson's construction

<!-- Generated by `./scripts/generate-docs.sh`. Do not edit: every step below is a
     sentence the implementation produced while running, and editing them here would make
     this file disagree with the code it documents. -->

Turns a regular expression into an ε-NFA. Each operator becomes a fragment with one
entry and one exit, so composing them is only ever a matter of adding ε-transitions — which
is why there is never a case analysis about how two pieces join, and why the output is larger
than a machine you would draw by hand.

## Worked example

Input: `(a|b)*abb`

1. Reading `a` moves from q0 to q1.
2. Reading `b` moves from q2 to q3.
3. Union: q4 can take either branch without reading input, and both branches rejoin at q5. This choice is the nondeterminism.
4. Star: q5 loops back to q4 to repeat, and q6 also reaches q7 directly — that last edge is what allows zero repetitions.
5. Reading `a` moves from q8 to q9.
6. Concatenation: once the first part finishes at q7, the second part begins at q8 without reading anything.
7. Reading `b` moves from q10 to q11.
8. Concatenation: once the first part finishes at q9, the second part begins at q10 without reading anything.
9. Reading `b` moves from q12 to q13.
10. Concatenation: once the first part finishes at q11, the second part begins at q12 without reading anything.
11. Done: 14 states, starting at q6 and accepting at q13.

**Result.** an ε-NFA with 14 states.

Every line above is a `Step` returned by the same function the editor calls. The
step-through at [/convert](https://kleene.pranavmshukla.in/convert) renders these sentences,
